questions.q: What does 'cold start' refer to in this lesson?
options: The time it takes to write a new Dockerfile
The delay between a new instance being asked to start and it actually being ready to serve a request
The delay before a rollback finishes
The time a load balancer takes to route its first request ever
questions.explain: Cold start is specifically the startup delay paid by whichever request triggers a new instance to spin up.

questions.q: Per this lesson, which step dominates an AI service's cold start time?
options: Starting the container process itself
Routing the request through the load balancer
Pulling a small base image
Loading model weights into memory or GPU memory
questions.explain: Model weights can be gigabytes, and loading them into GPU memory takes seconds to low minutes -- that's the step that dominates.

questions.q: How does this lesson characterize the typical cold-start duration gap between a web service and an AI service?
options: Web service: roughly 1-5 seconds; AI service: roughly 30 seconds to 2+ minutes
Both are typically around 1-5 seconds
Web service: 2+ minutes; AI service: 1-5 seconds
Neither service type experiences a measurable cold start
questions.explain: The lesson gives these approximate ranges specifically to show how much longer an AI service's cold start typically is.

questions.q: What trade-off does keeping a min-instances floor above zero make, according to this lesson?
options: It eliminates cold starts completely with no downside
It requires rewriting the application in a different language
It guarantees the model will never need to be reloaded
It pays for idle capacity around the clock in exchange for fewer cold starts
questions.explain: A min floor means some instances are always running, which costs money even when there's no traffic -- that's the trade-off.

questions.q: What trade-off does using smaller or quantized model weights make, per this lesson?
options: No trade-off at all -- it's a strictly free win
A real quality trade-off in the model itself, not just an infrastructure knob
It only affects build time, never runtime behavior
It requires switching cloud providers entirely
questions.explain: Smaller/quantized weights load faster but can change model output quality -- the lesson calls this out as a real quality trade-off, unlike the other two mitigations.
